newsitem.title: FRANCE: Egypt wheat sale in step with market - trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt wheat sale in step with market - trade.

text.p: A large sale of French wheat to Egypt at $140.50 to $143.90 per tonne, Fob, was cheap but not out of line with world markets, European grain exporters said on Monday.
They said the transaction reflected expectations of a further decline in world prices.

The sale was bound to put new pressure on the European Union to step up wheat export subsidies, they said, adding that the Commission would eventually do so as it could not afford to miss what might be one of the last substantial sales of old crop wheat, exporters said.
"This shows that the trade is very bearish on the market. It is also betting that the EU will go along as it did in the past," one exporter said.
On February 2, Egypt bought 450,000 tonnes of French wheat for delivery in February, March, and April at between $140.70 and $143.90 per tonne, Fob.
On Monday Egypt said it had bought an additional 50,000 tonnes of French wheat at $140.50 for April delivery
Egypt was initially seeking 50,000 tonnes of French, U.S. or Australian wheat.
Last Thursday the EU granted the export of 249,800 tonnes of EU soft wheat at a refund of 14.98 Ecus per tonne, which valued French wheat for late February at $150 per tonne, Fob.
The French wheat sale shows a discount of $10 over the last EU wheat award.
But several exporters said the Egyptian sale was in step with a decline in world prices amid weak demand and ample supplies from top grain exporters.
They said a sluggish export scene had pushed U.S. soft red wheat for March down to $146 per tonne on Friday.
Exporters estimatedthat the European Union needed to increase the subsidy on wheat exports by three to four Ecus per tonne to help cover the sale to Egypt.
Guy Legras, director general of agriculture at the EU Commission, however, recently ruled out a more aggressive stance on exports, saying the EU was satisfied with its export pace.

But exporters widely expect the European Union, which had a near record crop last year, to seize one of its last opportunity to make substantial exports before new North American supplies hit the market in the spring.
They said the Commission might not be prepared to grant overnight the refunds adequate for Egypt but would eventually relent, provided world prices continued to fall.
"It will happen. We just need to be patient," one exporter said.
Rouen wheat for February delivery was quoted at 855-860 francs per tonne, depending on silo, unchanged from Friday.
